rationale: Seed hypothesis proposes tubulin/MT-binding features in the DYF-3 CH domain. PMID:26912722 directly tested the IFT38 CH domain and found no tubulin binding; only IFT54 binds. Surface basicity of DYF-3 1-115 (net exposed +4) is unremarkable. Adding this would be CH-family over-annotation.

Same reasoning as GO:0008017. Fold similarity to the tubulin-binding IFT81 CH domain (TM 0.595) and IFT54 CH (TM 0.60-0.61) is not evidence of ligand, since those domains and IFT38 share the fold but differ in ligand.
Uninformative. If a curator wants an MF for dyf-3, prefer a specific IFT-B2 partner-binding statement by ISS from Chlamydomonas/mouse, or leave MF as ND.

Currently IBA plus ComplexPortal NAS. PMID:26980730 shows Cluap1/IFT38 is an integral component of the IFT-B peripheral subcomplex in mammalian cells, and PMID:26912722 reconstitutes IFT38 within IFT-B2. A curator could support this with ISS from those orthologue references, or add the child term for the peripheral/IFT-B2 subcomplex if the ontology provides one.

Supported by IBA alone (GO_REF:0000033, with A8BGV3, MGI:1924029). No C. elegans experimental support found, and no MTOC localisation in PMID:15713455. This is the one existing annotation that could be mistaken for microtubule-proximal function and may be phylogenetic carry-over from basal-body localisation of vertebrate CLUAP1.

Currently NAS from ComplexPortal only. PMID:17314406 profiles IFT particle motility in worm ciliary mutants and assigns components to IFT modules; PMID:20409822 lists DYF-3 (Qilin) among C. elegans IFT-associated proteins with measured axonemal velocities. A curator should check whether DYF-3::GFP IFT velocity data in those papers support an IDA or IMP.
IDA from PMID:15713455 (stunted cilia in dyf-3 mutants, cell-autonomous rescue) plus IBA/IEA/NAS. Well supported and is the core process.

term: chemotaxis / chemosensory behavior / response to alkaline pH
rationale: IMP from PMID:23664973. These are consequences of losing sensory cilia, not of a direct DYF-3 activity. Useful phenotype annotations, but they should not be read as the gene's core function.
